newsitem.title: GERMANY: WestLB sees DAX hitting 3,200 points in 1997.
newsitem.headline: WestLB sees DAX hitting 3,200 points in 1997.

text.p: Analysts at Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank on Wednesday predicted that the DAX index would hit 3,200 points this year, a rise of some seven percent from its current level.
"1997 will be a year for equities," WestLB Research chief Klaus Wieners told a news conference.

Wieners conceded, however, that the market's performance would not match that of the past year. For 1996, the bank is predicting earnings growth for DAX companies of 38 percent, slowing to a rise of 16 percent in 1997 and 15 percent in 1998.

The bank recommends overweighting the car, banking, chemical and utility sectors in the first quarter of 1997 and underweighting construction, trade and insurance, but said favourites would change as the year continued.
In 1998, autos, trade and engineering would show the fastest earnings gains, Wieners said.
